_comment: Phase 2b golden: the useState reel as a BUG HUNT (shorts/motion_themes.yaml). One narrator; the hook is the bug report, the breaks are clues, fix_idea names the culprit. Only the setup beat asks ("Can you spot it?"). The hook is a claim, not a question; hook_question is still the reel's question. Also the stub answer for the bug_hunt theme on useState material.
topic: Why does changing a plain variable not update the screen?
hook_question: Why does the like button stay stuck at zero?

shots.speech: There's a bug: this like button stays stuck at zero.

captions.text: There's a bug: this like button stays stuck at zero.

shots.visual: Bug report card over a phone mock; each tap on the like button fails and the count stays 0; status pill 'Still 0'.

shots.speech: The suspect is how React remembers your values.

captions.text: The suspect is how React remembers your values.

shots.visual: Title card: series label, 'useState', the promise line, three icon tiles.

shots.speech: Here's the code at the scene. Likes sit in a plain variable. Can you spot it?

captions.text: Here's the code at the scene.

shots.visual: Code window LikeButton.jsx with a dashed evidence outline; two lines highlighted in turn.

shots.speech: Clue one: every re-render runs your component again from the top. The variable starts fresh, back at zero.

captions.text: Clue one: every re-render runs your component again from the top.
The variable starts fresh, back at zero.

shots.visual: Entity card <LikeButton /> showing 1; a render sweep passes and the value drops back to 0; evidence tag '1'.

shots.speech: Next clue: changing a plain variable never tells React anything changed. So the screen never updates.

captions.text: Next clue: changing a plain variable never tells React anything changed.

shots.visual: Entity card above a system panel 'React: Idle'; the connector is broken with an x; evidence tag '2'.

shots.speech: The culprit is a missing use State. It keeps the value in React's own memory, safe across renders.

captions.text: It keeps the value in React's own memory, safe across renders.

shots.visual: Stamp 'CULPRIT' on a system panel 'React' that now holds a 'likes' slot; a pulse travels up the connector.

shots.speech: Swap in the setter, set Likes. Each tap updates React's memory, then React re-renders with the new value.

captions.text: Each tap updates React's memory, then React re-renders with the new value.

shots.visual: Trigger chip setLikes(1) sends a pulse to the system panel; the slot goes 0 to 1; the entity card re-renders showing 1.

shots.speech: The fixed line: use State of zero gives you the value and its setter.

captions.text: The fixed line: useState(0) gives you the value and its setter.

shots.visual: Code map card: likes -> memory icon 'the current value'; setLikes -> bolt icon 'updates it and re-renders'.

shots.speech: Case closed: every tap sticks, and the likes keep climbing.

captions.text: Case closed: every tap sticks, and the likes keep climbing.

shots.visual: The hook's phone mock again: each tap succeeds and the count climbs 1, 2, 3; stamp 'CASE CLOSED'.

shots.speech: Remember: re-renders reset plain variables. use State keeps the value. And the setter updates it and re-renders.

captions.text: And the setter updates it and re-renders.

shots.visual: Takeaway list: three rows with the refresh, memory and bolt icons.

shots.speech: Follow for more, one idea at a time.

captions.text: Follow for more, one idea at a time.

shots.visual: End card: Up next, Follow button, series chips.
